title: Equality of values in a residually transcendental curve extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of transcendence degree one [def-kun-transcendence-degree], with $K$ separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]. Let $O\subseteq L$ be a valuation subring and put $R=O\cap K$. Assume $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(R)}\kappa(O)=1$. Then for every $z\in L^\times$ there is $c\in K^\times$ such that $z/c\in O^\times$. In particular, if $z\in O\setminus\{0\}$, $c$ can be chosen in $R\setminus\{0\}$, and if $z\in\mathfrak m_O\setminus\{0\}$, it can be chosen in $\mathfrak m_R\setminus\{0\}$. Here a valuation subring $B$ of a field $F$ [def-weil-field] means a subring with fraction field $F$ such that, for every $z\in F^\times$, $z\in B$ or $z^{-1}\in B$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_B=B\setminus B^\times$ and its residue field is $\kappa(B)=B/\mathfrak m_B$ [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, first stage on p. 28: Abhyankar inequality and divisibility of the ground-field value group; stated without a choice of value-group notation. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this exact result.

proof.text: Put $\Gamma_L=L^\times/O^\times$ and $\Gamma_K=K^\times/R^\times$. The inclusion $K\subseteq L$ identifies $R=O\cap K$ as the induced valuation subring, and [lem-trf-abhyankar-inequality] applies with $F=K$, valued field $L$, and valuation ring $O$. Its residue-field term is the assumed $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(R)}\kappa(O)=1$, while $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=1$, so it gives $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_L/\Gamma_K)+1\le1$ and hence $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_L/\Gamma_K)=0$.

source.place: §2.1, Lemma 2.1.2 and Proposition 4.3.1 proof, p. 27; local archival copy unavailable

proof.text: By [lem-trf-rational-rank-zero-torsion], the quotient group $\Gamma_L/\Gamma_K$ is torsion. Thus for every class $\alpha\in\Gamma_L$ there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $n\alpha\in\Gamma_K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1 proof, p. 27: “In particular, the group G ... is a torsion group”; local archival copy unavailable

proof.text: By [lem-trf-separably-closed-value-group-divisible], $\Gamma_K$ is divisible. Fix $z\in L^\times$ and let $\alpha=[z]\in\Gamma_L$. Choose $n$ with $n\alpha\in\Gamma_K$, and choose $\beta\in\Gamma_K$ with $n\beta=n\alpha$. The value group $\Gamma_L$ is an ordered abelian group and therefore torsion-free, so $\alpha=\beta$. Choose $c\in K^\times$ representing $\beta$; then $z/c\in O^\times$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1 proof, p. 27: divisibility of $|K^\times|$ and equality $|R|=|O|$; local archival copy unavailable

proof.text: If $z\in O\setminus\{0\}$, the identity $c=z(z/c)^{-1}$ shows $c\in O\cap K=R$, so $c\in R\setminus\{0\}$. If moreover $z\in\mathfrak m_O\setminus\{0\}$ and $c$ were a unit of $R$, then $c$ and $z/c$ would both be units of $O$, forcing $z$ to be a unit, a contradiction; hence $c\in\mathfrak m_R\setminus\{0\}$.
